newsitem.title: USA: SEC clears Refco Securities plan to pay localities.
newsitem.headline: SEC clears Refco Securities plan to pay localities.

text.p: The Securities and Exchange Commission said Wednesday it approved a plan by Refco Securities, Inc. to distribute $3.25 million to defrauded clients of former California investment adviser Steven Wymer.

Wymer is serving a seven-year prison sentence after he plead guilty in 1992 to a massive investment fraud scheme that cost dozens of municipal clients in Colorado, Iowa and California roughly $174 million.

Refco was the principal broker-dealer that Wymer used to maintain client accounts. The firm in August 1996 settled SEC charges that it failed to supervise a former employee who allegedly helped Wymer defraud localities out of over $80 million.
SEC had alleged that the employee, Kimberly Goodman, passed false information about account balances to clients. She neither admitted nor denied the charges.
